ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.68 to the rider's original payment method for the uninformed off-route segment (Seg1); send the driver a notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route compliance record (no formal warning, first incident); no formal violation flag — driver has 0 upheld route deviations in 90 days.
ruling.reasoning:
Route deviation: actual 17.6 km vs optimal 13.3 km = +4.3 km [F1], well over the 1 km tolerance of RD-1, so RD-2 applies. The code isolates one off-route segment, 09:06–09:16, driving Kaki Bukit Rd 2 → … → Pipit Rd, +4.03 km [F3]. Total excess-distance billed is $5.95 for 4.22 km at $1.4103/km [F4]; surge is 1.0× so no surge component [F5].

Seg1 (F3) — counts, not exempt. The driver's chat notice named only a reroute "via Ubi Avenue 2" and the rider's "Sure, no problem" [F7, F8] is consent to that named road alone; consent is the rider's own message and was sent before the segment, so the notice/consent element is met only for Ubi Avenue 2. Ubi Avenue 2 does not appear among the roads actually driven (Kaki Bukit Rd 2, Kaki Bukit Ave 2, Eunos Link, Jalan Eunos, Changi Rd, Jalan Turi, Geylang Serai, Geylang Rd, Paya Lebar Rd, Circuit Link, Circuit Rd, Pipit Rd) [F3], and the driver admits in his own statement that he went by Jalan Eunos instead "because it looked clearer" [F10] — a driver choice, not the agreed route (RD-5: named road absent → not covered; the driver's claim of verbal agreement is not consent to a different road). The rider's complaint matches this [complaint]. So the segment is not exempt under RD-3/RD-5.

Traffic: the only congestion event is on Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway, band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 08:48–09:16 [F11] — that is evidence of traffic on the replaced part of the recommended route at trip time (RD-4), and it explains why the driver asked to reroute. But RD-4 never exempts a segment, and here the driver deviated to a road the rider never agreed to. Since congestion existed on the recommended route and the rider was not informed of, and did not agree to, the Jalan Eunos route, the outcome under RD-2 is refund of the excess distance fare (the "traffic reason, rider not informed" row), which is the same amount as the no-traffic row. The other traffic rows (Buangkok East Drive, Sengkang East Avenue, bands 5) [F12, F13] are on unrelated roads and give no reason [F14 no incidents; F15 weather fair].

Amount: refundable distance = 4.03 km (none exempt) × $1.4103/km = $5.68. Time fare, tolls/ERP and surge are not refunded (RD-2). This is a fraction of the billed excess of $5.95 because the billed figure used 4.22 km including map-matching noise under 0.2 km and non-segment distance.

Repeat check (RD-6): the driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute but route upholds = 0 and no-show = 0 [F17] — profile facts never decide the case, and there is no prior upheld deviation within 90 days, so no flag_account. Rider profile is clean [F16].

Precedent: DISP-001 (uninformed reroute, excess distance fare only) is aligned. Amount under $10 → system ruling final (TH-1 / C1).

segment_findings.reason: The driver's notice named only a reroute via Ubi Avenue 2 and the rider's pre-segment "Sure, no problem" [F7, F8] covers only that road (RD-5). The segment drove Kaki Bukit Rd 2, Eunos Link, Jalan Eunos, Changi Rd, Geylang Rd, Paya Lebar Rd, Circuit Rd, Pipit Rd — Ubi Avenue 2 is absent [F3], and the driver's own statement says he chose Jalan Eunos instead because it looked clearer [F10]. Driver-chosen off-route road the rider did not name → not exempt under RD-3/RD-5; the +4.03 km counts and is refundable under RD-2.

element_findings.element: RD-5 notice and consent to the off-route route
element_findings.reason: Notice was given before the segment (09:03 chat, segment 09:06–09:16) and the rider acknowledged, satisfying the timing requirement — but only for the named road Ubi Avenue 2. The road actually driven (Jalan Eunos) was the driver's own choice [F10], so rider consent does not cover the segment as driven.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's statement that the rider agreed to the reroute does not cover the road actually driven: his own words say he went via Jalan Eunos instead of the agreed Ubi Avenue 2, so his claim of consent to the driven route is rejected (RD-5: verbal/claimed agreement is not rider consent to a different road).

The congestion on Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway [F11] gives a traffic reason under RD-4 but never exempts a segment; since the rider was not informed of the Jalan Eunos route, RD-2 still awards the excess distance fare.
